originality.rationale: Substantive comparison to nearest known results (knowledge-cutoff, live web unavailable): Stanica-Maitra DAM 2008 gives g_n count formula, bounds and constructions but no complete Walsh-certified histogram or affine-sieved extremal table for all 2^20 RSBFs in n=7; Kavut-Maitra-Sarkar-Yucel ePrint 2006/449 heuristic search reports selected high-nl examples (balanced high-nl RSBFs in n=7,8,9) not exhaustive distribution with full spectra and systematic inequivalence sieving; Carlet book/chapters give general Walsh/nonlinearity theory and global covering radii RM(1,7)=56, RM(1,8)=120 but no RSBF-subclass distribution or extremal representatives. None implies exact 33-value histogram, count 11788 maximizers / 22344 next-maximizers, canonical lex-min ANFs with 128-point spectra, or 11/12 affine-class lower bounds. Internal SCOPE scan (3 successes on 4-uniform families, spider walks, J2-free rank; 3 failures on Szemeredi-Trotter, Polya-Vinogradov, dicyclic gaps) covers different objects/methods. Existence of some nl=56 RSBF was likely findable heuristically (density ~1.124%) and is not claimed as sole novelty; delta is completeness plus certificate-backed table. No priority claim is made in DRAFT; originality confidence was capped due to offline search. Failed-search does not establish priority; PASS rests on substantive non-implication, with residual risk of missed thesis/paper noted.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later as compact checkable reference, not textbook/parameter-substitution/tiny-gain/bare-enumeration: (i) RSBF-restricted covering radius of RM(1,7) equals unrestricted 56, with 11788 explicit maximizers including plateaued/semi-bent type |W|={0:64,16:64} of degree 4 weight 56 — a concrete coding/crypto fact (nonlinearity governs linear-cryptanalysis resistance) directly reusable for design; (ii) full 33-value distribution with per-value canonical ANF representatives, degrees, spectra, hex and orbit-sum expressions provides a lookup table no textbook gives; (iii) structural analysis beyond bare counts: degree distributions, 4 Walsh types and 5 acmax values in maximizers, 4xN types in next-max, 11/12 affine-class lower bounds via genuine invariants, weight symmetries, and gap pattern (steps of 7 below 44) prompting divisibility conjecture (explicitly unclaimed). Heuristic prior examples are subsumed and certified. Reproducible in seconds with published generator plus independent NumPy path.
